faq.a_accountant: Yes. Invite your accountant as a team member or a read-only user, depending on what they need to do. Accountants with several clients can use represented companies to manage them from one login.
faq.a_ai_plan: Core, Pro and Enterprise. AI reads supplier bills you upload, photograph or forward by email.
faq.a_archive: For the statutory retention period: 10 years in Slovenia and 11 years in Croatia. You can export your data at any time.
faq.a_available: Yes. Paply is in its testing phase and opening up step by step, and some businesses already use it every day. You can create an account and start on the Free plan today. Sending and receiving over the e-invoice exchange network is coming soon; until then invoices go out by email with a PDF.
faq.a_cancel: Yes. All paid plans are month to month with no lock-in. You can upgrade, downgrade or cancel from Billing in the app.
faq.a_card: No. The Free plan is free forever and lets you draft unlimited invoices, design templates and download PDFs. You only add payment details when you choose a paid plan.
faq.a_countries: Slovenia and Croatia, including fiscalization with each country's tax authority. Serbia is on our roadmap, and the apps are already available in Serbian.
faq.a_delete: Yes, at any time from your account settings. Invoices that must be kept by law stay in the archive until the retention period ends.
faq.a_diff: Fiscalization reports an invoice to the tax authority, which confirms it with a unique code printed on the invoice. E-invoicing sends the invoice itself to your customer as structured data instead of a PDF. They are separate obligations, and Paply is built to handle both.
faq.a_email_count: No. Only e-invoices sent or received through the exchange network count. Email delivery, drafts and PDF downloads are unlimited on every paid plan.
faq.a_fiscal_how: Upload your fiscal certificate once in the settings. From then on, Paply fiscalizes invoices when you confirm them and prints the codes and QR code on the invoice. If the tax service is down, Paply resubmits automatically.
faq.a_gdpr: Yes. Our privacy policy explains how we handle personal data, and our data processing agreement covers the data you process in Paply.
faq.a_mobile: Paply for Android and iOS is coming soon. It works with the same account as the web app, so anything you set up today carries over.
faq.a_mobile_buy: No. Plans are managed on the web at paply.app, and your subscription works in the app automatically.
faq.a_need_tech: No. In Paply you fill in a normal invoice form. Paply produces the right format for the country and keeps the archive for you, and once network exchange launches, it delivers the e-invoice for you too.
faq.a_network: Exchange over the e-invoice network is in its final stage of development and is coming soon. Your plan's network allowance applies from launch, and nothing changes in how you create invoices.
faq.a_over: Nothing stops working. Each e-invoice above your plan's allowance costs €0.12 and is added to your next bill. If you regularly go over, a bigger plan is usually cheaper.
faq.a_pay_methods: By card, through Stripe, in the Paply web app. Plans can't be bought inside the mobile app; your subscription from the web works there automatically.
faq.a_pdf: Not in the legal sense. An e-invoice is structured data, such as eSLOG or UBL XML, that software can process without a person retyping it. A PDF can still be used wherever the law doesn't require a structured e-invoice.
faq.a_switch: Yes. Import your partners, continue your invoice numbering from where you left off, and import invoices you already issued so your history and open balances are complete.
faq.a_vat: All prices exclude VAT, which is added on your invoice where it applies.
faq.a_what: Paply is invoicing software for businesses in Slovenia and Croatia. You create, send, receive, fiscalize and archive invoices in one place, on the web and soon on your phone. It's developed in Slovenia by ENZOR d.o.o.
faq.a_where: In the European Union, in Amazon Web Services' Frankfurt region. Passwords and certificates you connect are encrypted, and sign-in is protected by two-factor authentication.

guide.disclaimer: This guide is general information, not legal or tax advice. Rules and deadlines can change, so check your obligations with your accountant or the tax authority.
guide.formats_l1: eSLOG 2.0, the Slovenian national XML format, compliant with EN 16931.
guide.formats_l2: UBL 2.1, an international XML format used for Croatian e-invoices.
guide.formats_p1: The EU defined a common semantic model for e-invoices, EN 16931, so that invoices from different countries carry the same information. Each country then uses one or more technical formats built on it:
guide.formats_p2: You don't need to know any of this to use Paply: you fill in an ordinary invoice form and Paply produces the right format for the country.
guide.g_camt: Bank statement file formats. Import one into Paply and payments are matched to invoices.
guide.g_en16931: The European standard that defines what information an e-invoice must contain, so invoices can be read across borders.
guide.g_eor: Unique invoice identifier (enkratna identifikacijska oznaka računa) returned by FURS once it confirms the invoice.
guide.g_eslog: The Slovenian XML e-invoice format, aligned with EN 16931.
guide.g_furs: The Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia, which verifies invoices paid in cash or by card.
guide.g_hub3: The Croatian payment slip standard, printed as a 2D barcode that banking apps can scan.
guide.g_jir: Unique invoice identifier (jedinstveni identifikator računa) returned by the Croatian Tax Administration.
guide.g_kpd: The Croatian classification of products and services, used to classify items on e-invoices.
guide.g_oib: The Croatian personal identification number used for both people and companies.
guide.g_pain: The SEPA payment order file format. Paply creates one to pay several supplier bills at once in your online bank.
guide.g_tax: The Croatian Tax Administration, which fiscalizes Croatian invoices.
guide.g_ubl: Universal Business Language, an international XML format for business documents, used for Croatian e-invoices.
guide.g_upn: The Slovenian payment QR code. Scanning it in a banking app fills in the amount, IBAN and reference.
guide.g_zki: Protective code of the issuer (zaštitni kod izdavatelja) calculated for every fiscalized Croatian invoice.
guide.g_zoi: Protective mark of the issuer (zaščitna oznaka izdajatelja), a code calculated when a Slovenian invoice is issued.
guide.hr_d: Fiscalization 2.0 from 1 January 2026: e-invoices between businesses, fiscalization of all payment methods and what changes in 2027.
guide.lead: What an e-invoice actually is, how it differs from fiscalization, and what changes for businesses in Slovenia and Croatia. No jargon, we promise (well, there's a glossary).
guide.p_l1: Fiscalization with FURS (Slovenia) and the Tax Administration (Croatia), with the verification QR code on the invoice
guide.p_l2: Invoices by email with a PDF, from Paply or your own mailbox
guide.p_l3: UPN QR payment codes, bank reconciliation and a statutory archive
guide.p_l4: Sending and receiving structured e-invoices (eSLOG 2.0, UBL 2.1) over the exchange network
guide.pdf_d: Easy to send, but the recipient retypes it. Fine where it's still allowed, and Paply sends these today.
guide.rs_p: Serbia has its own national e-invoicing system with different rules from both. Support for Serbia is on Paply's roadmap for a later phase.
guide.si_d: FURS fiscal verification today and mandatory e-invoices between businesses from 1 January 2028.
guide.vs_l1: Fiscalization reports an invoice to the tax authority at the moment it is issued. The authority confirms it with a unique code that must appear on the invoice. In Slovenia this is FURS with the ZOI and EOR codes; in Croatia, the Tax Administration with ZKI and JIR.
guide.vs_l2: E-invoicing is about how the invoice itself travels from seller to buyer: as structured data over an exchange network rather than on paper or as a PDF.
guide.vs_p1: The two are often confused, but they are separate obligations with different purposes:
guide.vs_p2: One invoice can be subject to both. A good invoicing tool handles them in the same flow, so you never have to think about which rule applies.
guide.what_p1: An e-invoice is an invoice issued, sent and received as structured data, usually an XML file, that the recipient's software can read on its own. A PDF sent by email is an electronic invoice in the everyday sense, but it is not an e-invoice: a person still has to read it and type it into their accounting system.
guide.what_p2: Because every field (seller, buyer, VAT number, lines, VAT rates, totals, payment details) sits in a defined place, an e-invoice can be checked, booked, approved and paid automatically. That is why governments across the EU are making them mandatory between businesses.
guide.xml_d: Machine-readable XML, delivered through an exchange network straight into the recipient's system.

hr.a1: Paply fiscalizes invoices to consumers (F1) today. Exchanging structured B2B e-invoices over the network is coming soon. Until then, Paply sends invoices by email with a PDF.
hr.a2: From 1 January 2026, yes. F1 fiscalization covers every payment method, including bank transfers.
hr.a3: During 2026 you need to be able to receive e-invoices. From 1 January 2027 you also issue e-invoices for domestic business transactions.
hr.a4: Yes. The app, the invoices and the emails to your customers are all available in Croatian.
hr.f1_p1: When you issue an invoice to a consumer, it is sent to the Tax Administration as it is issued. Your system calculates a protective code (ZKI) and the Tax Administration answers with a unique identifier (JIR). Both are printed on the invoice together with a QR code customers can use to verify it.
hr.f1_p2: From 2026 this applies however the customer pays: cash, card, bank transfer or anything else.
hr.f2_p1: For domestic business transactions, invoices travel as structured e-invoices based on the European standard EN 16931 (in the UBL 2.1 format), through an information intermediary. Each line carries a product classification code (KPD).
hr.f2_p2: Both sides fiscalize the e-invoice: the seller when sending, the buyer when receiving. Businesses also report certain data, such as payments and rejected invoices, to the Tax Administration (e-reporting).
hr.lead: Since 1 January 2026, Croatian businesses exchange invoices with each other as structured e-invoices, and fiscalization covers every payment method. Here is what that means for you.
hr.ov_l1: F1: fiscalization of invoices issued to consumers. It now applies to every payment method, including bank transfers, not only cash and cards.
hr.ov_l2: F2: structured e-invoices between businesses (and to the public sector), which both the sender and the recipient fiscalize, together with e-reporting to the Tax Administration.
hr.ov_p1: Croatia's new Fiscalization Act, often called Fiscalization 2.0, applies from 1 January 2026. It splits invoicing obligations into two tracks:
hr.p_cta: You can start today on the Free plan and switch on fiscalization with a paid plan whenever you're ready.

si.a1: Fiscal verification applies to invoices paid in cash, which in Slovenia includes payment cards and similar methods. Invoices paid only by bank transfer are generally not verified with FURS. Check your specific case with your accountant.
si.a2: From 1 January 2028. Until then, you can keep sending invoices to businesses by email with a PDF.
si.a3: Yes. You add your premises and devices in Paply's settings, upload your FURS certificate, and Paply registers them and fiscalizes your invoices from then on.
si.a4: Yes. Paply is developed in Slovenia, and the app, invoices and customer emails are all available in Slovenian.
si.b2b_p1: From 1 January 2028 a PDF by email will no longer be enough between businesses. Invoices will travel as XML in the Slovenian eSLOG 2.0 format, aligned with the European standard EN 16931, so they go straight into your customer's accounting system.
si.b2b_p2: The good news: if your invoices already live in a proper invoicing tool, the switch is mostly invisible. You keep filling in the same form; only the delivery changes.
si.furs_p1: Before you can fiscalize, you register your business premises and electronic devices with FURS. When you issue an invoice, a protective mark (ZOI) is calculated and the invoice is sent to FURS, which returns a unique identifier (EOR). Both codes and a QR code appear on the invoice.
si.furs_p2: If FURS can't be reached, the invoice is still issued with its ZOI and must be submitted again later. Paply does that resubmission for you automatically.
si.h1: E-invoicing and fiscal verification in Slovenia
si.lead: Slovenian businesses already verify cash and card invoices with FURS. From 1 January 2028, invoices between businesses must also be structured e-invoices. Here is how to be ready.
si.ov_l1: Today: invoices paid in cash, which in Slovenia also includes cards, must be verified with the Financial Administration (FURS) as they are issued.
si.ov_l2: Public sector: invoices to public bodies have been sent as e-invoices for years.
si.ov_l3: From 1 January 2028: invoices between businesses must be issued and received as structured e-invoices.
si.p_cta: Start on the Free plan today and you'll be set up well before the 2028 deadline.
